title: Socio-Religious Reform Movements of the 19th Century

questions.question: Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj) in:
questions.rationale: The Brahmo Sabha was founded in August 1828 for worship of one formless God without idols or caste; the Atmiya Sabha of 1814 was his earlier discussion circle and the Tattvabodhini Sabha came in 1839.

questions.question: Sati was declared illegal in 1829 by Regulation XVII under which Governor-General, championed by Rammohan Roy?
questions.rationale: William Bentinck's Regulation XVII of 1829 made sati a culpable crime, following Rammohan Roy's petitions and shastric arguments against the practice.

questions.question: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856 was won mainly through the agitation of:
questions.rationale: Vidyasagar marshalled shastric citations and about a thousand signatures for the 1856 Act; the first legal remarriage followed within a year.

questions.question: Dayananda Saraswati's Arya Samaj, founded in 1875, took which as its battle-cry?
options: Service to mankind is service to God
One caste, one religion, one God
questions.rationale: 'Back to the Vedas' declared the Vedas infallible and all later additions — idolatry, caste by birth, child marriage — corrupt; the Satyarth Prakash (1875) set out the creed.

questions.question: Dayananda's Satyarth Prakash was published in the same year the Arya Samaj was founded:
questions.rationale: Both the Samaj (Bombay) and the Satyarth Prakash appeared in 1875; the D.A.V. College at Lahore followed in 1886.

questions.question: The Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Vivekananda in 1897, works under the motto:
questions.rationale: The motto means 'for one's own salvation and for the good of the world', joining Vedantic spirituality with famine relief, schools, and hospitals.

questions.question: Vivekananda's celebrated address at the Parliament of Religions ('Sisters and Brothers of America') was delivered at:
questions.rationale: At Chicago in September 1893 Vivekananda opened with 'Sisters and Brothers of America' and presented Vedanta to the West, leading to the Mission's founding in 1897.

questions.question: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society (1864) and the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College (1875), which became Aligarh Muslim University in:
questions.rationale: MAO College, opened at Aligarh in 1875, was raised to Aligarh Muslim University by an act of 1920, the culmination of the Aligarh Movement.

questions.question: The Satyashodhak Samaj ('Truth-Seekers' Society'), founded in 1873, was led by:
questions.rationale: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj at Pune in 1873 for caste equality, holding weddings without Brahman priests; he and Savitribai had opened a girls' school in 1848.

questions.question: The Theosophical Society moved its headquarters to Adyar, Madras in 1882; its most famous Indian-era leader, from 1893, was:
questions.rationale: Annie Besant arrived in India in 1893, led the Society, founded the Central Hindu College (1898) that became part of Banaras Hindu University, and later led the Home Rule League.
